analysis:
Examined two test-only changes. FlintAnswerStopTests.swift head line 130 adds `case .logprobs: break` to FlintStreamOutcome.record. FlintResponseFormatTests.swift line 362 (base and head) changes `case .info: break` to `case .info, .logprobs: break`. Both changes only make exhaustive switches compile after MLXServerGenerationEvent gained a new .logprobs case. Neither changes production behavior, constraints, encryption (T-008), the cache (T-041), or attestation and authorization (TB-011).

The new .logprobs event itself is an integration question for production code outside this batch. Logprobs can carry per-token information derived from A-001 plaintext. Production code must emit logprobs only on the encrypted response path. It must also apply the same answer-stop holdback and response_format suppression as content, so held-back or stripped stop text and private reasoning do not leak through logprob tokens. These tests discard logprobs and do not verify that suppression. No regression is identified in the supplied test units.
